notes: English content description: the page continues a statement claiming surjectivity of the map from the tame fundamental group of U_t to that of U. Its proof reduces connectedness of a covering on the special geometric fibre to the generic fibre, describes a smooth proper family with a codimension-at-least-two part and a relative normal-crossing divisor, and invokes purity and a specialization theorem. These are document claims, not verified theorems in this run. The bottom begins Remarque7 about Lefschetz pencils and stops after a cancelled phrase.

The prospective reference is literally “qui figure(ra) dans SGA 1 XIII (exposé de Mme Raynaud)”. It does not itself state that a proof step is unverified. The remark cites SGA 7 XVIII and number 6. These are references, not dates or page counts.

There is no independent title sheet, date, own page number, signature, or stated total page count. The handwritten bottom-left archive number is 114 and is encoded only as a comment. The text begins with the fragment “phisme évident”.

Every front-side text line, display and visible correction was compared against both witnesses in the two original half views. One whole view was used for layout, followed by one view of each original half, followed by seventeen distinct crops each viewed once. Neither a half nor a decided crop was reopened. No OCR, recognition library, PDF extraction, external source, other scan, other reader directory, or further agent was used.

Whole image dimensions are 1690×2160; each supplied half is 1690×1160. Half_b starts at whole-image y=1000. All reported crop boxes use original whole-image coordinates. The crop enlargement used only Pillow autocontrast and LANCZOS at 2600 pixels across; no rotations or sharpening were needed.

The retained written forms include “enx vertu”, “grassmanienne”, the grave on m in “croise-grave-m-ents”, and “figure(ra)”. No normalization to familiar French or a mathematically expected variable was used. The cancelled right-edge fragment is “famill”; an entirely clipped final e was not supplied.

The ambiguity in the first covering glyph, the g/v cell, the codimension cells, and the d/e cell is represented without an invented earlier/later correction order. The definite deleted text is tel que sa,; de; V de Y; f; connu; et voisin de t, la famill; and s quotients par. Cancellation of t in compte remains uncertain.

No mathematical inference resolved an ink choice. Repetition of V or the known role of the cover did not decide the initial U/V composite. The codimension inequality was decided from its two visible strokes. The parameter insertion was placed from its left leader, not from grammatical preference.

The closely repeated impressions in the initial m of maximale (c12) and the a of La (c13) were inspected because they initially looked crowded. No secure unlike-letter alternative was found, and plain m and a are retained. These are not treated as bold or a special alphabet.
The two detached points near en t prime are included as an uncertain inline drawing at their actual relative positions. Their origin, maker and textual purpose remain unassigned.

H’s emph/bold heading presentation is treated as editorial rather than as evidence of original typographic bold. Its underline-equivalent emphasis of surjectif and Remarque is not counted as a mere macro discrepancy. The lack of a handwritten wrapper by itself is likewise not a difference. There is no visible underline under Démonstration.
No unrelated prior-page quotation was present in the supplied prior-questions file. The supplied notation snapshot was read as instructed but was not treated as evidence overriding this scan.

No mathematical proof verification or computational check was performed; the checks array is intentionally empty. File-structure validation is a transcription-delivery check, not a mathematical check.
